q: Electricity is a form of ____.
e: Electricity is a form of energy. Energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: There are two types of electricity: electrostatics (or) static electricity and ____ (or) current electricity.
e: There are two types of electricity: electrostatics (or) static electricity and electrodynamics (or) current electricity. Electrostatics is charge at rest. Like charges push apart.

q: Electrostatics is the study of electric charge at ____.
e: Electrostatics is the study of electric charge at rest. Electrostatics is charge at rest. Like charges push apart.

q: Electrodynamics is the study of moving electric charges and their interaction with magnetic and ____ fields.
e: Electrodynamics is the study of moving electric charges and their interaction with magnetic and electric fields. The physics in this sentence is built around electric.

q: Electric charge is the physical property of matter that causes an electric force when placed in an ____ field.
e: Electric charge is the physical property of matter that causes an electric force when placed in an electromagnetic field. The physics in this sentence is built around electromagnetic.

q: Electric charges may be either at rest (static charges) or in ____ (moving charges).
e: Electric charges may be either at rest (static charges) or in motion (moving charges). The physics in this sentence is built around motion.

q: Flow of charges is called an electric ____.
e: Flow of charges is called an electric current. Current here means the flow of electric charge.

q: A French scientist, ____, studied the nature of electric charges possessed by substances and found that there were only two kinds of charges.
e: A French scientist, Du Fay, studied the nature of electric charges possessed by substances and found that there were only two kinds of charges. The physics in this sentence is built around Du Fay.

q: Benjamin Franklin named them positive charge which is represented by a plus sign (+) and negative charge by a ____ sign (-).
e: Benjamin Franklin named them positive charge which is represented by a plus sign (+) and negative charge by a minus sign (-). The physics in this sentence is built around minus.

q: Like charges ____ and unlike charges attract.
e: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. The physics in this sentence is built around repel.

q: The closer the charges are, the ____ the force between them.
e: The closer the charges are, the greater the force between them. The physics in this sentence is built around greater.

q: When two charged objects are brought together, they produce either attractive or ____ force.
e: When two charged objects are brought together, they produce either attractive or repulsive force. The physics in this sentence is built around repulsive.

q: The electric force between two charged objects is one of the ____ forces of nature.
e: The electric force between two charged objects is one of the fundamental forces of nature. The physics in this sentence is built around fundamental.

q: The electric force holds the particles that make up an ____ together.
e: The electric force holds the particles that make up an atom together. The physics in this sentence is built around atom.

q: Charged objects can exert forces to other charged objects without being in ____ with them.
e: Charged objects can exert forces to other charged objects without being in contact with them. The physics in this sentence is built around contact.

q: This is possible because there is an electric ____ around each charge.
e: This is possible because there is an electric field around each charge. The physics in this sentence is built around field.

q: In SI units, electric charge is measured in ____ (C), in honour of Charles Augustin de Coulomb, a French physicist.
e: In SI units, electric charge is measured in coulomb (C), in honour of Charles Augustin de Coulomb, a French physicist. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: He discovered that the force between two charged objects depends on the magnitude of their charges and on how ____ apart they are.
e: He discovered that the force between two charged objects depends on the magnitude of their charges and on how far apart they are. The physics in this sentence is built around far.

q: Since the magnitude of charge of an electron is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C, one coulomb of charge is equivalent to the charge of ____ electrons.
e: Since the magnitude of charge of an electron is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C, one coulomb of charge is equivalent to the charge of $6.25 \times 10^{18}$ electrons. The physics in this sentence is built around $6.25 \times 10^{18}$.

q: One microcoulomb ($1 \mu\text{C}$) = ____ C (one millionth of a coulomb).
e: One microcoulomb ($1 \mu\text{C}$) = $10^{-6}$ C (one millionth of a coulomb). The physics in this sentence is built around $10^{-6}$.

q: Charge is one of the ____ physical quantities.
e: Charge is one of the quantized physical quantities. The physics in this sentence is built around quantized.

q: It means that charge cannot take any arbitrary values, but only discrete values that are integral multiples of the fundamental charge that is charge of an ____.
e: It means that charge cannot take any arbitrary values, but only discrete values that are integral multiples of the fundamental charge that is charge of an electron. Electron here means the negative particle that orbits the nucleus.

q: The formula for quantized charge is $Q = ne$, where $Q$ = electric charge, $n$ = ____, $e$ = charge of an electron.
e: The formula for quantized charge is $Q = ne$, where $Q$ = electric charge, $n$ = integer, $e$ = charge of an electron. The physics in this sentence is built around integer.
